data.gender_notes: Marsiya is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Arabic name Marsiya refers to the state of submission and obedience to Allah. It is derived from the root 'asara', which means 'to be heavy' or 'to bear a great burden'. In the context of Islamic spirituality, Marsiya represents the woman's commitment to God and her willingness to carry the weight of her faith. The name Marsiya carries the meaning “A woman's submission to God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Marsiya usually hope their child will grow to embody a woman's submission to god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

The name holds spiritual significance and reflects the values of patience and resilience in the face of hardship. Across various Muslim cultures, Marsiya is used to commemorate the passing of a loved one or to express condolences.
